wording: In one neutral birth-death growth run to 5,000 cells, the cumulative count of subclonal mutations was approximately but not tightly linear in 1/f (R^2 = 0.958); the pre-registered criterion R^2 >= 0.98 was not supported.
counterevidence_limits: Single run, cell fractions without sequencing noise; the criterion may be too strict for one stochastic realisation. To be tested with replicates in x3.

wording: Across 10 replicates of DV0's neutral clonal-branching toy (5 at N = 5,000 and 5 at N = 20,000 cells), R^2 of the M(f) ~ 1/f fit ranged from 0.916 to 0.985 (medians 0.954 and 0.976); the pre-registered median >= 0.98 was not supported at either size, so DV0's single value of 0.958 was typical rather than an outlier.
counterevidence_limits: Cell fractions without sequencing noise; the 0.98 threshold is the agent's, not a published criterion; 4 extinct starts were restarted and are reported.
operationalization: Divergence = neutral branching clonal evolution (1/f signature)

wording: Explicit Euler on y' = -lam y converged for h lam = 0.5 to 1.9 and diverged for h lam = 2.1 and 2.5 (|y| about 2.6e12 and 6.7e52 after 300 steps), exactly as the amplification factor |1 - h lam| predicts: numerical divergence of a solver is a property of the method and step size, not of the system solved.
counterevidence_limits: Linear test equation only; no source on numerical analysis was read in this track.
operationalization: Divergence = numerical instability of an iterative method
